# zip-password-finder

zip-password-finder is a tool to find the password of protected ZIP files.

Features
- Supports both ZipCrypto and AES-encrypted ZIP archives.
- Dictionary attack (test passwords from a dictionary file, one word per line).
- Brute-force attack with configurable character sets and password length range.
- Multi-threaded workers to speed up the search.

Character sets available for brute force generation:

  l | abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz [a-z]
  u | ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ [A-Z]
  d | 0123456789                 [0-9]
  h | 0123456789abcdef           [0-9a-f]
  H | 0123456789ABCDEF           [0-9A-F]
  s | "space" and symbols

Usage

Run the program with the input protected ZIP file and options. Example help output:

Usage: zip-password-finder [OPTIONS] --inputFile <inputFile>

Options:
  -i, --inputFile <inputFile>                    path to zip input file
  -w, --workers <workers>                        number of workers
  -p, --passwordDictionary <passwordDictionary>  path to a password dictionary file
  -c, --charset <charset>                        charset to use to generate password
      --charsetFile <charsetFile>                path to a charset file
      --minPasswordLen <minPasswordLen>          minimum password length
      --maxPasswordLen <maxPasswordLen>          maximum password length
      --fileNumber <fileNumber>                  file number in the zip archive
  -s, --startingPassword <startingPassword>      password to start from
  -h, --help                                     Print help
  -V, --version                                  Print version

Examples

- Use a dictionary file to find a password:

  zip-password-finder --inputFile secret.zip --passwordDictionary words.txt

- Brute force with lowercase letters, length 1 to 6:

  zip-password-finder --inputFile secret.zip --charset l --minPasswordLen 1 --maxPasswordLen 6
